project: Orders: catalogue, customers, orders with discounts.
canonicalSource: Fowler, M. (2002). Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture. Addison-Wesley. Ch. 1 (Layering: presentation, domain, data source), Service Layer, Table Data Gateway, Money. Closed layering as in Buschmann, F. et al. (1996), Pattern-Oriented Software Architecture Vol. 1, "Layers".
styleDefinition: Three layers, closed (strict): presentation -> business -> persistence. Each layer uses only the layer directly below it.
Persistence (Table Data Gateways and plain records) knows nothing about the layers above; it returns rows, the business layer maps them.
The business layer (domain model, Service Layer) may hold and call persistence gateways: that is the normal downward dependency.

Presentation (controllers, views, router) sees business services and model objects only, never persistence; the business layer builds its own lower layer (ServiceFactory) so presentation never has to name it.
The business layer depends on no web or persistence framework.

noViolatingVariant.reason: No style-valid violation exists: in closed layering the business layer holding a persistence gateway is the intended dependency, so the template's binding (domain kind = business, infrastructure kind = persistence) has no violating case in this style. See RDQ-1.

outOfScope: Coupling metrics (FF-C*), SOLID proxies (FF-SO*), naming and convention rules (FF-CV*) and the neuronal functions (FF-N*) are not compared: they are threshold proxies or conventions (FR-V6 makes them advisory), and they say nothing about whether a planted architectural violation is caught. The runner lists their rows separately as unscored.
